answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making the fee to mint an identity rise with the total count already on the ledger. Minting the k-th key costs a base fee times k, read from a monotonic public counter, so one honest agent pays a small early fee while a sybil minting N clones pays a bill growing as N squared. The kernel of the rule is a counter anyone can audit; on a barren tundra of free slots a vine of clones grows quadratically expensive until its cost overtakes its lifetime reward. The ledger enforces the fee, capping mass minting below a reward/cost bound, not a rich attacker.
